messages:
Maya S: ping — AcmeOps reported a flood of 401s against their Dedicated Private endpoint after they enabled the new L7 load balancer in front of Istio. They say requests that used to work with API key are suddenly returning unauthenticated. Can someone help triage?

ops-admin: repro from their host (sanitized):
```
> POST /v1/completions HTTP/1.1
> Host: private.redwood.acme.acmeops
> Authorization: Bearer <token>
> Content-Type: application/json
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< content-type: application/json
< {"error":"unauthenticated","message":"missing auth header"}
```
They are definitely sending Authorization.

Maya S: I checked the ingress access logs on the Istio gateway pod. The Authorization header is not present in the recorded headers. Example access log line:
```
remote=10.20.5.77 method=POST path=/v1/completions status=401 req_id=xyc789 headers=[x-request-id:xyc789,x-forwarded-for:10.10.2.4,host:private.redwood.acme.acmeops]
```

Ben K: Did they introduce any extra proxy (NGINX or internal TLS terminator) in front of the Istio ingress? Those often rewrite/remove headers by default.

ops-admin: They rolled an NGINX sidecar to do TLS termination for the LB -> Istio handoff. The platform team says only cert rotation but we'll double-check configs.

Ravi N: Can you run a local test from inside the istio-proxy container to see if the proxy is forwarding Authorization? E.g.:
`kubectl exec -it istio-proxy-xxxxx -- curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer testing" http://127.0.0.1:15000/anything`
If header disappears there, it's an Envoy chain issue. Also tcpdump on the pod could confirm whether the header is present on the wire.

Maya S: Ran the local curl in the sidecar. Header present to 15000, but when forwarding to the app (port 8080) the Authorization header is gone. So removal happens inside the Envoy filters.

Ben K: Two usual suspects: an explicit EnvoyFilter (or istio AuthorizationPolicy) removing headers, or the upstream NGINX rewriting them. Please list EnvoyFilters in the ingress namespace and any cluster-level filters.

Maya S: Found an EnvoyFilter that looks suspicious — it was intended as generic header hardening. Snippet: 
```
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: EnvoyFilter
metadata:
  name: global-header-sanitizer
spec:
  workloadSelector:
    labels:
      istio: ingressgateway
  configPatches:
  - applyTo: HTTP_FILTER
    match:
      context: GATEWAY
    patch:
      operation: INSERT_BEFORE
      value:
        name: envoy.filters.http.header_sanitizer
        typed_config:
          "@type": type.googleapis.com/...
          headers_to_remove:
            - "authorization"
            - "cookie"
            - "x-forwarded-proto"
```
This was added in an infra cleanup PR last quarter. It matches `istio: ingressgateway` label which our Dedicated Private ingress also uses.

Ravi N: That explains it. The filter was meant for hosted plane gateways only but the workloadSelector is too broad and picks up customer ingress.

Maya S: I tested by temporarily removing the EnvoyFilter from the customer's namespace. After removal the Authorization header appears in the app logs and calls succeed (200). Customer confirmed working.

Ben K: For immediate mitigation: scope the EnvoyFilter to hosted-only gateways. Suggest patch: set workloadSelector labels to include `plane: hosted` and limit namespace to `redwood-system` in `match`. Example: 
```
workloadSelector:
  labels:
    istio: ingressgateway
    plane: hosted
# and add match.namespace: redwood-system
```
Apply to hosted cluster only.

Ravi N: Long-term controls: 1) add a deploy-time linter that flags EnvoyFilters with broad selectors (e.g., matching ingressgateway without plane or namespace), 2) include a canary test that deploys the filter to a canary namespace and runs a simple curl asserting Authorization is forwarded to backends, 3) document that filters touching gateways must explicitly opt-in to private/dedicated planes.

Maya S: Filed INC-2026-322 for audit. I'll send the customer a short post-deploy note and the config diff. Also opened an infra PR to scope the filter and add the linter.

infra-bot: rollback global-header-sanitizer in namespace acme-dev... ROLLBACK SUCCESS :white_check_mark:

ops-admin: verified end-to-end, all good on our side. Thanks so much.

Ben K: Follow-up action items:
- PR to change workloadSelector + add namespace match (assigned to Ravi)
- Add gate test + linter rule in infra repo (assigned to Ben)
- Postmortem note explaining why cluster-level filters are dangerous for dedicated/private customers (Maya)

Maya S: Closing thread once PR merges. Will paste PR link in the incident ticket. Thanks team!
